rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉⲃⲟⲧ 'month.' The hierarchical sequence in this kephalaion (years > X > days > hours > moments) where X is described as longer than days but shorter than years, decisively identifies ⲃⲉⲧⲉ as 'months.' Each cosmic 'power of X' begets offspring with X-proportionate lifespans.
Variant orthography of ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'years' (in accumulated vocabulary); ⲡ for ⲙ before ⲡ. Confirmed by parallel usage in lines 1, 18 with same sense as ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ in line 19.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲁϩⲉ from ⲁϩⲉ 'stand, age, lifetime.' Recurs as ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲍⲉ 'their lifetime' (lines 4, 7), ⲡⲁⲍⲉ 'the lifetime' (lines 5, 10, 14-15). Central organizing concept of this kephalaion's argument about progressive shortening of life-spans.
Coptic ⲕⲁⲗⲁϩⲏ 'womb' (cf. Crum). Confirmed by collocation ⲧⲕⲁⲗⲁⲍⲏ ⲛⲧⲟⲩⲙⲉⲩ 'the womb of their mother' at line 31-32 — the long-lived ancients spent a great chronos in their mother's womb before birth.

Same root as accumulated ⲁⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲏⲏⲥ 'support, foundation.' Here used three times (lines 14, 21, 29) as the existence-base or vital substrate of the generations: the first generations were 'pure in their support' while the latter 'have grown small in their support.' The 'support' = the cosmic life-and-light substrate that makes generation possible.
Cognate with ⲇⲱⲭⲃⲉ 'diminish' (in accumulated vocabulary); the ⲟ̄ⲱ- prefix may indicate perfect/completed aspect. Used here of years that have grown short, paired with ⲥⲃⲁⲕ 'become small.'
Probable Lycopolitan reflex on a root meaning 'far, long' (cf. ⲱⲓⲁⲩ, ⲟⲩⲏⲩ). Antithetic pair-partner with ⲥⲃⲁⲕ 'become short' — the ancients' years 'became long' while the latter ones 'became short.'
Verbal noun designating the act/process of decrease. Forms the abstract counterpart to verbs of shortening (ⲥⲃⲁⲕ) in this kephalaion's vocabulary of cosmic decline.

Lycopolitan ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ 'this word/saying' (= ⲡⲉⲓ̈ⲥⲉϫⲉ); ⲭ for ϫ is regular Lyc. Word division spans line 26-27 break. Construction ⲕϣⲓⲛⲉ ⲥⲁ ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ 'thou seekest after this saying' is standard discourse-marker.

Likely imperative or conjunctive of ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ 'proclaim, declare' (in accumulated vocab). Possible parsing ⲕⲁ- as imperative prefix, or ⲉⲕⲁ-ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ as future used as polite request: 'declare/may you declare to us.'
